key_insight: The paper argues that AI safety needs new mathematics across multiple fields to make AI systems understandable, controllable, and cooperative with humans.
engineering_relevance: For engineers building AI systems, the message is that safety is not just a systems problem but also a foundation problem requiring tools from logic, probability, algebra, and geometry.
method: Organize AI safety questions by mathematical discipline.
Map each field to a core safety target: cooperation, world-models, learned features, and training/generalization.
End each section with an open problem for mathematicians
evidence_signal: The abstract describes an invitation-style survey rather than reporting experimental data, so the support is conceptual and problem-driven rather than empirical.
watch_item: Because the paper is a conceptual roadmap, its ideas need concrete formalization and validation before they can be turned into deployable safety methods.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
